modules.title: From customer need to a controlled tool design
modules.subtitle: Learn what must be known before anyone chooses a flute or opens a program.
objectives: Separate component requirements from tool dimensions
Read a drawing using reference surfaces and tolerances
Build a reviewable specification for one real SKU

sections.heading: Two different manufacturing jobs
sections.body: CTC makes a cutting tool. Its customer then uses that tool to make a component. A Rollomatic grinder removes material from the tool blank to create cutting edges; the customer's drilling, routing or milling machine uses those edges on the workpiece. Their machine programs, settings and acceptance tests are different. First ask which component feature the tool must produce: a hole, slot, pocket, contour, chamfer or finished surface. A tool that matches its drawing can still fail the customer's process.

sections.heading: Write the application before drawing the tool
sections.body: Use a one-page application brief. Record workpiece material and condition, the feature and stock to remove, acceptable size and surface condition, access restrictions, machine and spindle, holder and overhang, coolant or extraction, batch volume, and the current failure. For PCB work add the laminate construction, copper, board stack, entry and backing materials, hole or routed-feature requirement, and downstream quality criteria. Treat these as fields to establish with the customer, rather than assumptions about a customer product.
bullets: Goal: what customer outcome must improve—yield, burrs, hole quality, cycle time, tool life or cost per acceptable part?
Constraint: which limits must never be traded away?
Evidence: what measurement or trial will show the requirement was met?

sections.heading: Understand the drawing's contract
sections.body: A nominal dimension is the intended value. A tolerance defines permitted variation. A datum is an agreed reference used to locate or orient other features. Keep shank diameter, cutting diameter, flute length, overall length, corner geometry and relevant angles unambiguous. Define the measurement location and method for tiny edges or complex profiles. A beautiful 3D image does not specify inspection acceptance. Tool Sketcher can produce drawing views and annotations from a VirtualGrind Pro simulation; the designer must still select the correct requirements.

sections.heading: Connect decisions to revisions
sections.body: Create a small design record linking the customer brief, drawing revision, material grade, geometry, manufacturing route, inspection plan and trial outcome. Record why a choice was made, including rejected choices and their evidence. Separate an experimental revision from the released production revision. A proposed change to the edge, coating, material or process needs its effect reviewed across manufacturing and customer use; visual similarity is not proof of equivalence.

sections.heading: Your shop-floor assignment
sections.body: Choose one frequent SKU and ask the designer, operator, quality engineer and application engineer to walk through the same requirement. Ask: Which dimension controls the customer's result? Which requirement is missing from the drawing? Who approves a revision? Capture disagreements as questions to resolve. Release evidence should include the agreed brief, approved drawing, feasible manufacturing route, measurable acceptance criteria and named owner. This checklist is a proposed learning framework, not a claim about CTC's current procedures.

exercise.prompt: A customer says: ‘Make the drill last longer.’ List the missing information before proposing geometry.
exercise.answer: Establish the drilled material and stack, hole requirement, machine/holder/runout, operating method, current tool and failure evidence, agreed end-of-life criterion, baseline life and acceptable tradeoffs. Then define a controlled comparison.

quiz.question: What does a drawing-compliant tool prove by itself?
options: The inspected tool characteristics met the stated drawing acceptance rules
The customer will achieve the desired life on every machine
The cutting program needs no trial
quiz.explanation: Manufacturing conformance and performance in the customer's process are separate claims and require separate evidence.

modules.title: How a carbide blank becomes a cutting tool
modules.subtitle: The wheel, machine motion and coolant together create the edge.
objectives: Describe blank preparation, fluting and relief grinding
Distinguish abrasive, grit, bond, truing and dressing
Explain why a drawing alone cannot reproduce the manufacturing process

sections.heading: Start with the blank
sections.body: A blank is the unfinished material from which the tool is made. Its carbide grade, dimensions, straightness, internal coolant features if present, and batch identity matter. Preparation establishes shank and stepped diameters, shoulders or necks before or alongside edge generation. Rollomatic's ShapeSmart family is associated with cylindrical pinch-and-peel grinding. A later tool-grinding operation creates the flutes and the surfaces that meet to form each cutting edge. The exact route varies with the tool and available equipment.

sections.heading: The wheel is a cutting tool too
sections.body: A grinding wheel contains many abrasive particles. For cemented carbide, diamond abrasives are a common choice. Grit size describes particle size; the bond holds the particles. Resin, vitrified and metal bonds have different behavior in retention, porosity and wear. Wheel profile, abrasive concentration and conditioning also affect the result. Do not reduce wheel selection to ‘finer means better’: productivity, heat, form retention and edge quality interact. Use the actual supplier specification and proven process for the application.

sections.heading: Motion creates geometry
sections.body: The machine moves and rotates the blank relative to the wheel. Those coordinated motions create helix, flute cross-section, core, rake and clearance. The rake face is the surface over which the chip flows; clearance prevents the tool surface behind the edge rubbing excessively. Different operations and wheel orientations create different surfaces. Wheel access and interference can make an apparently simple geometry hard to manufacture. Inspect a section through the simulated tool as well as its outside shape.

sections.heading: Condition the wheel and control the contact
sections.body: Truing restores the wheel's shape and its concentric running. Dressing changes the condition of its abrasive face, exposing or modifying cutting points. They are related but distinct. The permitted conditioning method depends on the wheel construction. Coolant must reach the wheel–blank contact; delivery, filtration and thermal stability are part of the process, not background utilities. A worn profile, loaded wheel, poor clamping or changing coolant condition can cause variation even when the program is unchanged.

sections.heading: Observe one tool through the route
sections.body: Ask an operator to identify the wheel and operation that produces each critical surface on a sample. Ask how wheel geometry is measured, when it is conditioned, how wear compensation is determined, and what triggers inspection. Compare the blank, simulated tool and measured first article. Preserve the wheel specification and offsets, setup and support details, coolant requirements, program revision and inspection results with the process record. Never infer spindle speed, infeed or coolant settings from this lesson; these require the installed machine's documentation and an approved process.

exercise.prompt: A flute becomes shallower across a batch although the nominal program is unchanged. What evidence would you collect?
exercise.answer: Verify the measurement first, then review the wheel profile and wear, dressing/conditioning history, offsets and compensation, blank dimensions, clamping/support, thermal conditions and sequence of inspected tools. Compare trends before altering geometry.

quiz.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes truing and dressing?
options: Truing concerns wheel geometry and running; dressing concerns the abrasive face condition
Both mean changing the tool drawing
Dressing guarantees the wheel has the correct profile
quiz.explanation: A wheel may have the right profile but poor cutting condition, or a sharp face but the wrong profile. Both need appropriate control.

modules.title: Manufacturing a PCD cutting edge
modules.subtitle: Understand the diamond, its support, the joint and the finishing route.
objectives: Distinguish a PCD segment from the supporting body and braze
Compare grinding, EDM and laser machining at a conceptual level
Identify release evidence for joint and edge integrity

sections.heading: PCD is a material, PCB is an application
sections.body: PCD means polycrystalline diamond. PCB means printed circuit board. A PCB tool is named for what it machines; a PCD tool is named for its cutting material. These categories can overlap but are not synonyms. A common PCD construction uses a diamond layer supported by carbide, with a segment joined to a prepared tool body. Other architectures exist: veined blanks integrate diamond regions into a carbide blank and do not require the same separate-segment braze route.

sections.heading: The joint belongs in the design
sections.body: For brazed construction, the pocket, support and segment positioning must allow the required edge geometry after finishing. The braze is a joining alloy between the prepared surfaces. Element Six's brazing guidance emphasizes designing the joint, controlling preparation and cleanliness, selecting compatible alloy and flux or atmosphere, and controlling heating and cooling. Temperature exposure matters to superhard materials. There is no universal braze cycle: the selected materials, joint and process must be qualified together. Check alignment, braze flow, cracks, chips, delamination and visible joint defects after joining.

sections.heading: Three ways to create an edge
sections.body: Grinding removes material with abrasive contact and can finish functional surfaces. Electrical discharge machining, or EDM, removes material through controlled electrical discharges; its applicability depends on the material's electrical behavior and the specific machine. Wire EDM is also used to cut suitable PCD blanks into segments. Laser machining removes material with focused light, offering access to geometries that can be difficult with a wheel. These methods may be combined in a route. A segment-cutting operation is not automatically the final cutting-edge preparation.

sections.heading: Compare outcomes rather than process labels
sections.body: Evaluate final edge radius, chipping, surface condition, profile accuracy, retained diamond volume, cycle time and subsequent finishing needs. Coarse and fine PCD grades do not respond identically. Laser source and pulse regime matter; do not apply one machine's capability to all lasers. Rollomatic lists LaserSmart machines for ultra-hard tool manufacture, but that does not establish that CTC owns one. Neither ‘laser’ nor ‘EDM’ alone is evidence that an edge is suitable for the customer's cut.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence through the route
sections.body: Ask: Where does the PCD blank come from? Which grade and layer construction are specified? Who defines the joining procedure? Which operation creates the final edge? What inspection detects a weak joint or damaged edge? Retain supplier and batch identity, segment layout, approved joining procedure, finishing program, inspection images and cutting-trial result. Use close-up images before and after cutting to distinguish a manufacturing defect from wear generated in service. The listed supplier examples describe their own products and processes, not CTC's qualified limits.

exercise.prompt: A new PCD tool has the right outside diameter but an edge breaks early. Why is a diameter check insufficient?
exercise.answer: It does not establish edge integrity, local geometry, diamond grade, support or joint quality. Inspect those features, review the manufacturing record and confirm the customer's engagement, runout and operating conditions before assigning a cause.

quiz.question: Which is the best reason to choose between grinding, EDM and laser processing?
options: Measured suitability of the resulting edge and qualified route for the application
The newest machine must always give the longest tool life
quiz.explanation: Material, geometry, process and customer conditions jointly determine suitability. A process name is not a release criterion.

modules.title: Your Rollomatic software and machine workflow
modules.subtitle: Place Tool Sketcher in the right part of the chain.
objectives: Explain what Tool Sketcher does and where its geometry originates
Trace one released drawing to its program and measured tool

sections.heading: Start from what is actually known
sections.body: This lesson introduces Rollomatic machines and Tool Sketcher. Before applying it, identify the installed machine models, software versions, licenses, options and exact file formats. The descriptions here reflect official public product pages reviewed on 23 September 2026. They are an orientation to product roles; they are not an inventory of CTC equipment or a promise that every advertised function exists in your installation.

sections.heading: The direction of Tool Sketcher matters
sections.body: Rollomatic describes Tool Sketcher as creating 2D drawings from 3D tool simulations directly in VirtualGrind Pro. It offers complete-tool, profile, core-section, blank and detail views, with dimensions and tolerances. Its public page lists DXF and PNG drawing exports. The stated relationship is programmed/simulated tool → drawing. Do not assume that importing a customer drawing automatically reconstructs the 3D tool or produces a validated machine program. Inspect the actual editable source behind a CTC drawing.

sections.heading: Know the product families
sections.body: GrindSmart is Rollomatic's cutting-tool grinding family. VirtualGrind Pro is its tool-programming environment, with tool examples and editable operations. ShapeSmart concerns cylindrical blank and punch grinding, including pinch-and-peel processes; ShapeSmart Pro is associated programming software. LaserSmart machines process ultra-hard materials using lasers; Rollomatic's software catalog describes LaserSuite simulation and beam-trajectory review. These roles are related but their equipment, programs and process physics differ. Match each claim to the exact model and installed version.

sections.heading: Walk through a complete job
sections.body: Begin with the approved requirement and drawing revision. Open the associated source program with a qualified operator. Identify blank, wheel or laser setup, clamping, support, operations and compensation. Review the simulated geometry and machine motion in the appropriate vendor tools. Produce and inspect a first article using the approved shop procedure. Resolve deviations through controlled changes, then release the associated drawing, program and setup together. Simulation is valuable evidence of intended geometry and motion; it does not prove actual wheel condition, machine calibration or cutting performance.

sections.heading: What an AI project needs to discover
sections.body: Ask someone to demonstrate how a changed core diameter travels from the editable design to a new Tool Sketcher section, a new program revision and a measured tool. Determine which data can be exported in documented formats and which actions require an operator. Ask Rollomatic about supported interfaces and permissions rather than assuming an automation API exists. For every SKU preserve a traceable relationship between the customer requirement, editable source, released drawing, setup, manufactured lot and customer trial.

exercise.prompt: You receive a PNG exported from Tool Sketcher. What must you obtain before using it as the basis for repeatable manufacture?
exercise.answer: Obtain the controlled drawing revision and requirements, its editable source program and applicable software version, the intended machine and setup, and inspection/validation evidence. A raster image alone does not carry the complete manufacturing definition.

quiz.question: What direction does Rollomatic explicitly document for Tool Sketcher?
options: VirtualGrind Pro 3D tool simulation to a 2D drawing
Any customer sketch to an automatically validated CNC program
Measured tool to a guaranteed cutting-life prediction
quiz.explanation: Tool Sketcher documents simulated tool geometry. Additional design, manufacturing and validation work remains necessary.

modules.title: Prove the tool is correct—and that it works
modules.subtitle: Metrology, measurement trust, process variation and customer trials.
objectives: Separate calibration, measurement-system studies and process capability

sections.heading: Measure the feature that matters
sections.body: Metrology is the science and practice of measurement. Tool diameter, flute form, runout, edge radius and surface finish are different characteristics and may need different instruments or setups. Runout describes how a feature varies as the tool rotates relative to a reference axis. State the datum, location, magnification or filtering where relevant, fixturing and acceptance rule. A measured number without its method can be difficult to compare with another instrument or the customer's result.

sections.heading: First establish trust in measurement
sections.body: Calibration relates an instrument's indication to a reference; it does not by itself prove that operators can repeatedly measure this tool feature. A gauge repeatability and reproducibility study examines variation when measurements are repeated and conditions such as operators change. Include representative parts, relevant geometry, re-fixturing and the intended working conditions. Also consider bias, resolution, drift and longer-term stability. A tiny display increment is not the same thing as small measurement uncertainty.

sections.heading: Then study the manufacturing process
sections.body: Plot critical measurements in production order to look for drift, shifts and unusual variation. Capability compares a stable process with engineering specification limits. Cp describes spread relative to tolerance; Cpk also reflects how close the mean is to a limit. The interpretation depends on adequate data, measurement quality and distribution assumptions. Do not advertise a capability value from a handful of favorable parts or combine different revisions into a single flattering number. Customer or internal approval criteria must define the required evidence.

sections.heading: Run a fair cutting trial
sections.body: Write the trial objective and end-of-life rule before cutting. Compare against a known baseline on representative material and equipment. Record the tool revision, holder, runout, workpiece batch, engagement, speed, feed and coolant/extraction. Measure customer outcomes: acceptable features produced, finish, burrs or damage, time and failure mode. Use multiple tools and suitable randomization or blocking to avoid confusing a material batch or machine shift with a design improvement. A tool removed while still working provides incomplete life information; record that explicitly.

sections.heading: Close the loop
sections.body: A release package should link the approved specification, material and process traceability, first-article results, trusted measurement method, production-control plan and customer trial. Preserve both passing and failing trials, including photographs and stop reasons. Ask: Can a different operator measure this edge the same way? Does quality see failures before shipment? Can we reconstruct the exact design used in a returned tool? Which customer outcome decides replacement? For AI, trustworthy labels and comparable trials are more valuable than a large folder of disconnected drawings.

exercise.prompt: One new tool makes 1,200 acceptable holes; one baseline makes 1,000. Can you claim a reliable 20% life improvement?
exercise.answer: Only an observed difference in those two trials is established. Review comparable conditions, failure/stop rules and measurement quality, then test enough independent tools under a suitable design to estimate variation and uncertainty.

quiz.question: What should you establish before interpreting Cpk as evidence of a capable process?
options: A suitable measurement system, stable process and justified data/assumptions
Only that the average dimension matches the drawing
quiz.explanation: Capability is a statement about process variation relative to limits, not simply about one good tool or its average dimension.

processSteps.title: 1. Define the customer operation
processSteps.body: Establish material, feature, machine, workholding, quality target and baseline failure. Distinguish PCB application from PCD cutting material.
processSteps.check: Approved application brief and measurable success criteria

processSteps.title: 2. Design the tool
processSteps.body: Select material and geometry, establish datums and tolerances, assess manufacturability, and record the reasons for design choices.

processSteps.title: 3. Prepare the blank
processSteps.body: Verify material and batch, establish shank and stepped diameters or prepare the PCD segment/body architecture.

processSteps.title: 4. Join PCD where required
processSteps.body: For a brazed design, follow the qualified preparation, joining and cooling procedure; verify joint and segment condition.
processSteps.check: Joining record and acceptance evidence; not every PCD construction needs this step

processSteps.title: 5. Generate the cutting geometry
processSteps.body: Use the qualified grinding, EDM or laser route. For grinding, control wheel geometry and condition, setup, motion and coolant.
processSteps.check: Approved machine program, setup and process revision

processSteps.title: 6. Finish and inspect
processSteps.body: Apply specified edge preparation, polishing or coating only where the design calls for it; inspect critical geometry and edge condition.
processSteps.check: First-article and lot results tied to a trusted measurement method

processSteps.title: 7. Validate in the customer's cut
processSteps.body: Run a planned comparison on the relevant machine and workpiece. Track acceptable output, quality, cycle time, wear and end-of-life reason.
processSteps.check: Documented application trial with baseline and uncertainty

processSteps.title: 8. Release and learn
processSteps.body: Release the drawing, program, setup and acceptance plan together. Connect production and field outcomes to the exact revision.
processSteps.check: Traceable release package and controlled change history
